item.text:
**6B.1 Research Note**

Bottom line: mixed, leaning no. There is real evidence that Sisi’s 2024 government treated welfare as important in specific policy areas, especially cash transfers, women’s empowerment, education, and refugee services. But most of the strongest positives are technocratic, partner-backed, or targeted safety nets, while the broader 2024 record still shows repression of economic dissent, exclusion of refugees, and heavy propaganda/self-justification. That makes “human welfare as a core purpose of rule” look partial and instrumental rather than clearly primary.

**Evidence supporting a welfare-centered reading**
- [World Bank Group Statement of Support to Egypt’s Development and Reform Efforts](https://www.worldbank.org/en/news/statement/2024/03/18/world-bank-group-statement-of-support-to-egypt-s-development-and-reform-efforts) | World Bank Group | 2024-03-18 | The World Bank said Egypt’s reform agenda aimed at “building better lives and opportunities,” with explicit emphasis on inclusive social protection, health, education, resilience, and protecting the poorest and most vulnerable. IDs: 6B.1, 5B.10, 5B.9, 5B.8.
- [Frequently Asked Questions on Egypt and the IMF](https://www.imf.org/en/countries/egy/egypt-qandas) | IMF | 2024 | The IMF said the program expanded targeted social protection, including Takaful and Karama coverage for over 5 million households, plus wage and sector-targeted support. That is strong evidence of welfare protection, though still within an externally supervised stabilization package. IDs: 6B.1, 5B.9, 5B.10, 5B.8.
- [Promoting Inclusive Human Capital Development and Building Resilience in Egypt through Cash Transfer Programs](https://www.worldbank.org/en/results/2024/05/28/promoting-inclusive-human-capital-development-and-building-resilience-in-egypt-through-cash-transfer-programs) | World Bank | 2024-05-28 | The Takaful and Karama program was described as institutionalized, well-targeted, and linked to health, education, child nutrition, and women’s empowerment, with a 55 percent benefit increase in 2023/2024 to cope with inflation. IDs: 6B.1, 5B.8, 5B.9.
- [Women's Empowerment Strategy 2030](https://sis.gov.eg/en/media-center/strategies/womens-empowerment-strategy-2030/) | State Information Service | 2024-03-12 | The presidency assigned the Women’s Empowerment Strategy 2030 to the government and state agencies as a working document, and the strategy explicitly framed equal opportunity, labor participation, legal protection, and social empowerment as state priorities. IDs: 6B.1, 5B.8.
- [House of Representatives approves drafted Social Solidarity bill](https://sis.gov.eg/en/media-center/news/house-of-representatives-approves-drafted-social-solidarity-bill/) | State Information Service | 2024-12-01 | The government-drafted Social Solidarity bill aimed to unify support programs and empower the most needy people “to ensure a decent life for all.” That is direct welfare language, though it is also official self-presentation. IDs: 6B.1, 5B.8.
- [Launch of the Joint UN Programme under the Joint Platform for Migrants and Refugees in Egypt](https://www.unhcr.org/eg/news/launch-joint-un-programme-under-joint-platform-migrants-and-refugees-egypt) | UNHCR Egypt | 2024-09-30 | The government, UN, and EU launched a program to support health and education for refugees and migrants in vulnerable situations, explicitly citing increasing needs after Sudan’s crisis. IDs: 6B.1, 5B.8, 5B.10.
- [Education Cannot Wait, UNHCR, UNICEF, Strategic Partners Call for Increased Resources for the Education Response in Egypt and Region](https://www.unhcr.org/eg/news/education-cannot-wait-unhcr-unicef-strategic-partners-call-increased-resources) | UNHCR Egypt | 2024-08-22 | The source says the government had taken notable steps to provide refugee education access. That is a real inclusion signal, even though resources were still inadequate. IDs: 6B.1, 5B.8.
- [Minister: Labor ministry has strategy to empower women](https://sis.gov.eg/en/media-center/news/minister-labor-ministry-has-strategy-to-empower-women/) | State Information Service | 2024-03-23 | The labor ministry said women’s economic empowerment and equal labor-market participation were top priorities at Sisi’s direction, with training programs and a gender-equality unit. IDs: 6B.1, 5B.8.

**Evidence against a welfare-centered reading**
- [Egypt: Halt crackdown on people voicing concerns over economic crisis](https://www.amnesty.org/en/latest/news/2024/05/egypt-halt-crackdown-on-people-voicing-concerns-over-economic-crisis/) | Amnesty International | 2024-05-13 | Amnesty documented arrests of people criticizing prices, workers striking for the minimum wage, and protesters blaming Sisi for “starving” the poor. That suggests the regime treated welfare complaints as threats to be suppressed, not as core feedback to govern by. IDs: 6B.1, 5B.9, 5B.7.
- [Egypt: More than 100 arbitrarily detained over calls for anti-government protests](https://www.amnesty.org/en/latest/news/2024/07/egypt-more-than-100-arbitrarily-detained-over-calls-for-anti-government-protests/) | Amnesty International | 2024-07-18 | Amnesty said 119 people were detained after calls for protests over price hikes and power cuts. This is strong evidence that economic pain triggered coercion rather than a welfare-first response. IDs: 6B.1, 5B.9, 5B.7.
- [Egypt: Education Restricted for Refugees](https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/12/02/egypt-education-restricted-for-refugees) | Human Rights Watch | 2024-12-02 | HRW found tens of thousands of refugee and asylum-seeking children out of school because of residency requirements, costs, discrimination, and lack of free public education. That undercuts a claim of broad human-welfare concern across vulnerable groups. IDs: 6B.1, 5B.8.
- [Egypt: Authorities Must End Campaign of Mass Arrests and Forced Returns of Sudanese Refugees](https://www.amnesty.org/en/latest/news/2024/06/egypt-authorities-must-end-campaign-of-mass-arrests-and-forced-returns-of-sudanese-refugees/) | Amnesty International | 2024-06-19 | Amnesty documented mass arrests, cruel detention conditions, and forced returns of Sudanese refugees without asylum access. This is strong contrary evidence for welfare across vulnerable groups. IDs: 6B.1, 5B.8.
- [Human Rights Watch World Report 2024: Egypt](https://www.hrw.org/world-report/2024/country-chapters/egypt) | Human Rights Watch | 2024 | HRW reported harsh prison conditions, denied family and lawyer access, and refusal to reopen the economist Aymad Hadhoud case. That points to welfare being secondary to control when vulnerable people were politically inconvenient. IDs: 6B.1, 5B.9, 5B.7.
- [National Human Rights Strategy](https://sis.gov.eg/en/media-center/strategies/national-human-rights-strategy/) | State Information Service | 2024 | The state’s own human-rights messaging includes anti-violence and anti-extortion campaigns, but it is still official framing rather than independent proof that welfare consistently outweighed regime survival. IDs: 6B.1, 5B.9.

**Synthesis**
- The strongest pro-welfare evidence is real but narrow: cash transfers, women’s empowerment, education access, and refugee service delivery.
- The strongest anti-welfare evidence is also real: repression of people complaining about living standards, exclusion of refugees from education, and harsh treatment of asylum seekers.
- My read is that Sisi did not govern in a purely indifferent or extractive way, but human welfare was not clearly the overriding core of rule. It was often treated as a managed sector, a stabilization necessity, or a legitimizing narrative rather than a consistently primary purpose.

Search gap: I did not find strong direct evidence of Sisi personally articulating human welfare as the central purpose of rule in 2024 in a way that went beyond standard regime messaging. The best positive material is programmatic and institutional, while the best negative material is concrete coercion against economically distressed people and vulnerable refugees.
